correctness.rationale: The two immediate proper factors of a minimal absent word must occur. If both share one complete gap, that gap's unique starting phase aligns the occurrences and forces the proposed word to occur. Four zeros always leave a common complete gap, and three zeros with either nonempty exterior run do too. With exactly three zeros and no exterior runs, the two proper factors require x,y in S, y≤s(x), x≤p(y), and absence is y≠s(x). For two zeros, a missing full gap is minimal exactly when both shortened runs are allowed (including 00); for an existing gap, both nonempty exterior runs are forbidden by the common anchor, and the one-sided overrun must exceed its allowed run by exactly one with its other proper factor tested by dominance. One zero has a dominance test on both immediate deletions, with only positive flank lengths capable of minimal absence. Zero zeros gives 1^{M+1}. The disjoint cardinality formula follows. An independent literal periodic-language scan checks all words up to the safe period-length-plus-one horizon (a longer candidate's proper factors agree on a full period), not a horizon derived from the predicted families. It matched 157 gap profiles (rotation representatives up to six consecutive gaps plus irregular examples) and the 10 versus 11 contrast. Replay python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py 4.
residual_risks: The frozen checker uses a formula-dependent cap and prints a final marker even if the consecutive-gap check returns early on a mismatch. The all-gap proof and the independent finite checks do not rely on that marker or cap.
No bound by three zeros is inferred for repeated gaps.
